messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@verityhealth.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@verityhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Security intake: SOC2 scoping, GDPR/HIPAA notes & FedRAMP path

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth:

1) Current state you asked about
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for our hosted inference control plane (report available to customers under NDA). We can scope additional product surfaces (Dedicated, Private, logging/observability) for expanded SOC coverage — this is commonly done as a scope expansion.
- GDPR/Data residency: We support EU-region deployments and can provide data residency details and DPA language.
- HIPAA: We execute BAAs for covered workloads; legal can share the template and typical redline history.

2) What Verity asked us to validate on the call
- Scope: Which environments do you want covered? (hosted API only / dedicated pools / private VPCs / all of the above)
- Data types: Confirm PHI / pseudonymized data / logs retention expectations.
- Timeline: initial intake -> evidence package -> decision window.

3) Proposed immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
- Ben Carter (security) to run a technical deep-dive and start the SSQ intake. Target: schedule 60m session next week. (Ben)
- Ben to share our SSQ response template and the current SOC 2 summary PDF for review. (Ben)
- Neha (legal) to share BAA template and flag any mandatory contract clauses that typically affect timeline. (Neha)
- Tessa (CS) to draft a mutual action plan with milestones for SOC 2 scope expansion and evidence delivery; target MLP in 2 weeks. (Tessa)
- Verity to confirm scope and provide their vendor security questionnaire (if you already have it, please attach). (Samira / Tom)

4) High-level timelines (ballpark)
- SSQ intake & initial evidence: 1–2 weeks
- Scope expansion & control validation: 4–8 weeks depending on breadth (e.g., adding Private deployments typically needs additional evidence collection)
- FedRAMP exploratory discussion: we can start discovery now but realistic engagement would be Q4 planning if Verity intends to pursue an ATO program.

Attachments included: vendor_ssq-verity-2026.xlsx (placeholder you shared), redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf (high level controls map).

If that aligns, Ben will kick off the SSQ intake and we'll follow with a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock the plan: 

- Scope confirmation: we need coverage for Hosted API and Dedicated pools that will process clinical scheduling PHI. Private (on-prem) can be considered later.
- Retention: logs retention expectation is 365 days for audit purposes — will that impact evidence collection?
- Data residency: Verity requires EU-region for EU patients; can you confirm which artifacts prove regional isolation?

We will:
- Share our completed vendor questionnaire (attached) and the internal priority matrix for the items we need validated. (See attached: verity_vendor_questionnaire_filled.xlsx)
- Put preliminary decision deadline at July 15 so we can align with procurement cycles.

Please ask Ben to include specifics on KMS/HSM handling and whether tokenized embeddings are considered PHI under your current control descriptions. Also, if Redwood has any objection to our standard BAA redlines, flag early so legal teams can triage.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we can do the deep-dive Tuesday at 11am PT if that works for Ben.

—Samira

Thanks — scheduling confirmed: Tuesday 2026-06-22 11:00am PT (60m technical deep-dive). I created a tentative calendar invite and included the scope doc template.

Quick notes and commitments from security side:
- SSQ intake: I'll start by sharing our SSQ response template (attached: ssq-response-template.xlsx). Samira, we'll ask you to mark priority controls (MUST / NICE) so we can focus validation.
- SOC 2 scope expansion: We can map controls for Dedicated pools and Private deployments; evidence collection typically includes configuration screenshots, policy artifacts, and audit logs. Expect ~2 weeks to assemble the initial bundle once scope is locked.
- KMS/HSM: We use customer-separable KMS integration for Dedicated and Private deployments; I'll prepare a short note on key handling and associated evidence.
- Embeddings & PHI: We'll cover how we treat transient model inputs, KV cache behavior, and options for minimizing PHI in telemetry during the deep-dive.
- FedRAMP: I will coordinate an internal note on the feasibility and initial ask path; agree that Q4 is the practical window for exploratory FedRAMP conversations.

Attachments I uploaded to the shared Drive: redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf (public summary), ssq-response-template.xlsx. Internal risk note (internal-risk-note.txt) referenced in private folder — will not share externally unless cleared by legal.

Neha: please confirm the BAA template we should send and any clauses that usually prolong negotiations. Tessa: once Samira confirms scope, can you draft the MAP with the July 15 decision date?

Samira / Tom: please confirm if Tuesday 11am PT works and if there are any additional folks (networking, privacy) who should join.
